findings: BASELINE MEASURED AT START (not inherited): book-budget 70 books / 42,770 words; L8 FAIL 70 vs bar 112; every other row PASS. book-stats p10 122 / p25 235.8 / median 614.5 / p75 837.8 / p90 1317.3 / max 1525. Our gap to Morrowind is at BOTH ends: too many scraps under 150 (15.7% vs 8.7%) AND nothing above 1525 against their 4090. The middle is over-full.

SKILL TAG CENSUS (re-derived, agrees with r2): 32 tags on 10 skills — speechcraft 7, root-speech 6, mercantile 6, survival 4, athletics 3, alchemy 2, acrobatics 1, security 1, warding 1, blades 1. L7b IS A RANK TEST AND THE RANK MOVES WITH CORPUS SIZE. Top third of 70 is rank <= 24; at 112 it is rank <= 38. Adding 42 books LOOSENS the bar proportionally, so existing tags are not at risk from dilution — but a new book that heavily uses another skill's vocabulary can displace an existing tagged book. SKILL_TERMS shares 'parry' between blades and shieldcraft, and 'keeper'/'tree'/'root' between root-speech and everything set in the marsh.

SOURCE MATERIAL FOR MARTIAL PROSE IS ALREADY ON DISK AND NOBODY HAD WRITTEN ABOUT IT: game/data/weapons/roster.json is 87 named weapons in 15 classes with 28 named LINEAGES each carrying a one-line mechanical character (splitter vs hatchet: 'they hook a shield rim rather than splitting it'; flail: 'cannot be stopped once started'; zwei: 'held further up the ricasso, so it turns over faster'). classes.json carries reach_m, arc_sweep_deg, r1_startup, poise_dmg and a per-class `problem` string. offhand.json has five shields, and the Xanmeer door greatshield CANNOT PARRY EVER by design, with a guard-angle rule that makes an out-of-angle hit unblocked at full damage. That is a whole martial argument the library can have without inventing a fact.

CONTRADICTION EDGES DO NOT NEED A REGISTRY FACT. book-stats S4 only requires `contradicts[].book` to resolve and S9 requires the `on` subject's content words to appear in BOTH texts. So a martial dispute can be built without touching canon-facts.json (another piece's file). All 37 existing edges carry `cf`; mine will not, and that is legal by the checker and cleaner by ownership.
S8 REQUIRES topics_taught SLUG WORDS TO APPEAR STEMMED IN THE BOOK'S OWN PROSE. Topics must be phrases the text actually uses.

Em dash is a CONFOUND not a tic (Morrowind writes '--'), normalised 1.0x — do not chase it.

THE FORD ALREADY HAD A CANON AND IT IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I WAS GOING TO INVENT. a-short-account-of-the-pacification gives 3E 391, a relief column of the Ninth, 200 at muster / 49 at the far bank, cause a flood surge, plus an appendix of arithmetic on the weir ponds; the-account-the-marsh-keeps answers it with 151-in-their-books against a-dozen-in-ours and names a woman at Lilmoth who says the loss was the carts; the-drowned-ford is a 72-word Argonian scrap about a woman who understood water. S6 (register variance) CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT AND IT WAS MINE. Mean-sentence-length IQR fell 6.6 -> 5.2 the moment 42 books landed: 28 of the 42 sat between 13 and 19 words per sentence, because I had written a serjeant, a hunter, a quartermaster, an Anvil gentleman and a staff historian at the same pace, and the pace was mine. Repaired by RE-VOICING ten texts — six clipped (a file-leader's unsent letter, a claw teaching, a lock manual, a marching manual, a serjeant at 47, a cohort clerk) and four periodic (an Office minute, a bowyer, a rice-cutter, a blade repairer) — not by adding books at the extremes, which the arithmetic shows does not move a quartile at all. IQR back to 6.6.

A CONCURRENT AGENT TURNED book-stats S4e RED MID-RUN AND THE FIX BELONGED ON MY SIDE. canon-facts.json grew from 6 disputed facts to 20 at 16:48; the new CF-D009 position B cites 'The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volumes the Second and Third' — a correct citation to two volumes of one work — and no single book title matched it, because the three volume titles put a comma where the series name ended and a colon before the subtitle. Re-punctuated the three titles so the SERIES name resolves on its own. Nothing else in the tree references those title strings (grepped).

RI-LOR03 §2's TAXON MINIMUMS CANNOT ALL BE MET AT ITS OWN CORPUS TARGET, and nobody has said so. The ten taxon rows are labelled minimums and sum to 122 (16+10+14+16+10+12+12+10+6+16) against a stated target of 112 texts. So the table is internally inconsistent as written, and any corpus that hits 112 must be short on some row by arithmetic. Where the martial expansion landed: T4 11->24 (target 16, met), T6 4->14 (12, met), T10 14->18 (16, met), T1 6->12 (16), T7 7->9 (12), T3 7->9 (14), T2 3->6 (10), T8 4->5 (10), T9 4->5 (6), T5 3->4 (10). The item's own provenance note already asks whoever next owns §2 to decide its numbers deliberately rather than inherit them; this is a third thing on that list.

CROSS-CUTTING QUOTAS after the expansion: 36 Argonian-authored (bar >=14), 34 declared contradiction pairs (bar >=8), 20 books wrong on purpose (bar >=6), quest-hint ratio 0.0% (bar <=10%), 5 multi-volume series (bar >=3). Fourteen of the 34 pairs are new and none of them carries a `cf` — they are method disputes rather than registry facts, which book-stats S4 permits and which keeps canon-facts.json (another piece's file) untouched.

THE EXPANDED LIBRARY EXPOSED A WIDOW THE BALANCING PASS COULD NOT REACH, and it is a defect in the paginator rather than in the writing. paginateBook()'s same-count pass re-runs paginate() with a smaller line budget and STOPS at the first cap whose page count changes — and for a long book that is the very first iteration, because a 16-page book gains a 17th the moment one line comes off every page. So the pass does nothing at all on long books. Measured over the 113 texts in a real browser: the-duelling-pick-and-the-bog-rapier ended on a page of ONE WORD, standing-instruction-for-auxiliaries on 18 and the-articles-of-the-wet-ledger on 21. A one-word page is exactly what RI-UIX05 §A B8 forbids. Fixed with two guarded fallbacks that only run after the existing pass has failed: (a) allow exactly one extra page and take the largest tail; (b) if even that has no candidate, split the final SPREAD evenly between its two pages, which keeps the page count. Result measured in the browser: 757 -> 769 pages, minimum page 1 word -> 10 words (and the 10 is a pre-existing 74-word scrap, not a widow), K1 still in band at p10 85.8 / median 121 / p90 154. The change cannot touch a book whose tail already clears the floor.

ALL FIVE SHIPPED W1-LIBRARY PROBES ARE GREEN ON THE 113-TEXT LIBRARY AND ON THE PATCHED PAGINATOR, in a real browser: w1-library-skillbooks PASS (59 tagged books recorded, 42 raised the named skill by exactly 1, the rest correctly clamped by RI-PRG03 §4's rest rule, 59/59 idempotent, control moved no skill, grant survives save/load), w1-library-r2-reading 6/6, w1-library-turns K5/K6/K7 PASS, critic-w1-library-pages 113/113 opened, boot-check PASS. So the 26 new skill_book tags are game objects and not labels — reading one really does grant a level.

notes_for_successor: The library is 113 texts and every row of book-budget (22) and book-stats (16) is green. Two honest shortfalls against Morrowind's measured shape are reported and NOT hidden: median 694 vs 535 (the corpus's middle was already full) and max 3,316 vs 4,090 (one outlier volume, which I would not pad to reach). The single row with least margin is book-stats S6 at 6.6 against a bar of 6 — it is a CORPUS statistic, so the next agent to add a batch of same-voiced books will fail it, and the remedy is re-voicing, not adding books at the extremes (moving a book past a quartile shifts it by one position, and the values around both quartiles are densely packed).
